author: slava77
body:
This came up in the context of developing some alpaka code with O(100) columns total visible in the translation units.

`GENERATE_SOA_LAYOUT` is expensive in the preprocessor. SoA-heavy translation units take GBs of memory and tens of seconds in macro expansion alone, and at GCC's default `-ftrack-macro-expansion=2` (developer areas, PR tests) they can exhaust GCC's macro location space, e.g. `RecoTracker/LSTCore/src/alpaka/LST.cc`. The level 2 setup tracks all expansions and has a limit of 2 location tokens per compile unit. The exhaustion is silent, or, depending on the include order, shows up as errors in unrelated headers (boost's `__LINE__`-based concept checks: "conflicting declaration"). IBs and releases avoid part of the cost with `-ftrack-macro-expansion=0`
(cms-sw/cmsdist#10848, #10868), PR [and developer builds do not](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmsdist/pull/10868#issuecomment-6964349005).

A synthetic test with `int32_t` columns shows scaling with the number of columns (n) of about 4 + 8.1n + 0.17n MB for the macro map location size (from `-fmem-report`).

Two causes:
1. In 56 of the ~76 passes over the elements, each element is guarded by    `BOOST_PP_GREATER(BOOST_PP_TUPLE_ELEM(0, TYPE_NAME), _VALUE_LAST_COLUMN_TYPE)`. Boost.PP compares by looped  subtraction: ~750 macro expansions per element and pass.
2. `BOOST_PP_SEQ_FOR_EACH` carries the remaining sequence through several macro layers per step, a term quadratic in the number of elements in the macro locations GCC tracks.

Changes (`SoACommon.h`, `SoALayout.h`; public macros and generated code unchanged):
- Type tests as lookup tables (`BOOST_PP_CAT` on the type code): `_IS_NOT_COLUMN` (the 57 guards), `_IS_SCALAR`,
  `_IS_BLOCK_TYPE` (was `BOOST_PP_LESS_EQUAL`), and `_SWITCH_ON_TYPE`. An `#error` fires if the type codes change; a new  code without table entries does not compile.
- `_ITERATE_ON_ALL`: a for-each dispatched on the element count, one expansion per element. Capacity 128 elements  (was 64 through `BOOST_PP_VARIADIC_TO_SEQ`, with a cryptic paste error beyond); above it, a clear compile error. The largest layout in CMSSW today has 47 elements. The iterated macros do not use the `R` argument (now `~`).
- `_ITERATE_ON_ALL_COMMA`: a direct sequence-to-list conversion instead of   `BOOST_PP_TUPLE_ENUM(BOOST_PP_SEQ_TO_TUPLE(...))`.


Effect (GCC 14, serial-backend object compile with the scram flags, one core; old -> new):

| file | level 2 (developer default) | level 0 (IB/release) |
|---|---|---|
| RecoTracker/LSTCore/src/alpaka/LST.cc | 26.2 s, 4.4 GB -> 8.8 s, 1.5 GB | 21.7 s, 0.86 GB -> 8.7 s, 0.75 GB |
| RecoParticleFlow/PFClusterProducer/plugins/alpaka/PFClusterSoAProducerKernel.dev.cc | 13.6 s, 2.9 GB -> 8.4 s, 0.9 GB | 12.2 s, 0.78 GB -> 8.1 s, 0.67 GB |
| synthetic layout, 40 `int32_t` columns (`-fsyntax-only`) | 4.4 s, 1.28 GB -> 1.0 s, 0.22 GB | |

For the synthetic layout: 2.73 M -> 0.26 M macro expansions, 600 MB -> 53 MB of macro location maps.

#### PR validation:

- **Exactness:** old and new headers give token-identical preprocessed output (`-E -P`; whitespace, `__FILE__` and the  `__LINE__` of asserts normalised) for 127 headers of the 36 packages using `GENERATE_SOA_LAYOUT` /  `GENERATE_SOA_BLOCKS`, 14 other SoA-heavy sources (incl. `LST.cc`, the `DataFormats/Portable` tests) and the SoATemplate tests; with GCC, the CUDA tests also with nvcc, part of the files also with clang.
- **Builds** (CMSSW_20_1_X_2026-11-17-1100, el8_amd64_gcc14), serial + CUDA: DataFormats/SoATemplate, RecoTracker/{LSTCore, LST, PixelTrackFitting}, RecoParticleFlow/PFClusterProducer, RecoLocalCalo/HcalRecProducers. ROCm compile of DataFormats/SoATemplate (incl. `.hip.cc` tests) and RecoTracker/LSTCore.
- **Unit tests** (GPU tests on an NVIDIA A30): DataFormats/SoATemplate 12, RecoTracker/LSTCore 1,  RecoParticleFlow/PFClusterProducer 15: all pass (the ROCm tests were not run: no AMD GPU).
- A 128-element layout compiles; 129 elements give the error message.
- `code-format`, `code-checks`, `check-headers`: clean.

No change in any output is expected: the preprocessed code is identical.


---

### Note for the author of cms-sw/cmssw#52085 (AoS layout)
 
@Electricks94 

Heads-up about an overlap: this PR rewrites the iteration and type-test macros extended by #52085.
- Expect only textual conflicts in `SoALayout.h`, next to the rewritten guards.
- #52085 adds ~24 more `BOOST_PP_GREATER(BOOST_PP_TUPLE_ELEM(0, TYPE_NAME), _VALUE_LAST_COLUMN_TYPE)` guards; with this PR  they become `_IS_NOT_COLUMN(BOOST_PP_TUPLE_ELEM(0, TYPE_NAME))` (same result; otherwise each costs ~750 expansions per  element again).
- The new `_ITERATE_ON_ALL(_COMMA)` / `_SWITCH_ON_TYPE` uses work unchanged and get cheaper; iterated macros must not use  the `R` argument.
- Since the AoS wrapper roughly doubles the number of passes, combining it with this PR keeps the compile cost of SoA  users from doubling. The preprocess-and-compare scripts are available for checking a rebase.
title: SoATemplate: lower the preprocessor cost of GENERATE_SOA_LAYOUT
